overview: Germany is a country in Central Europe and the most populous member of the European Union. Its capital and largest city is Berlin. After the Second World War, Germany was divided into West and East Germany; the Berlin Wall fell in 1989 and the country reunited in 1990. Germany is a federal republic of 16 states and has one of the largest economies in the world.

geography.text: Germany's landscape rises from north to south. The north is a flat plain facing the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. The centre has wooded hills and low mountains, and in the far south the Alps rise along the border with Austria, where the Zugspitze is the country's highest peak. Its great rivers include the Rhine, the Elbe and the Danube.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mild, damp winters in the north and colder, snowier winters in the south and the mountains.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Red deer and wild boar live in the forests, and wolves have returned in recent years.

history.text: For centuries the German lands were split into hundreds of states within the Holy Roman Empire. Germany was unified in 1871. After defeat in the First World War, the Nazis took power in 1933, started the Second World War and carried out the Holocaust. Divided after 1945 into West and East Germany, the country was reunited in 1990.

events.title: The Reformation
events.text: Martin Luther's protest against the Church begins the Protestant Reformation.

events.title: Unification
events.text: The German states unite as the German Empire.

events.title: Nazis take power
events.text: Adolf Hitler becomes chancellor and creates a dictatorship.

events.title: Defeat and division
events.text: Germany is defeated and divided by the Allied powers.

events.title: Berlin Wall
events.text: East Germany builds a wall dividing Berlin.

events.title: Reunification
events.text: East and West Germany are reunited.

government.text: Germany is a federal republic of 16 states, each with its own government. Voters elect the Bundestag, the national parliament, which chooses the Chancellor, the most powerful person in the government. The President is head of state but mostly has a ceremonial role. Germany's constitution, the Basic Law, dates from 1949.

economy.text: Germany has the largest economy in Europe. It is famous for engineering and manufacturing, especially cars from companies such as Volkswagen, BMW and Mercedes-Benz, as well as machinery, chemicals and electrical goods. Many of its firms are medium-sized family companies that lead the world in a narrow speciality.

culture.text: Germany is the land of composers such as Bach, Beethoven and Brahms, of the writer Goethe, and of Gutenberg, whose printing press transformed Europe around 1450. The Brothers Grimm collected fairy tales such as Hansel and Gretel and Snow White. Munich's Oktoberfest is the world's largest beer festival.

items.title: Gutenberg's press
items.text: Printing with movable metal type began in Mainz around 1450.

items.title: Brothers Grimm
items.text: Their collection of fairy tales was first published in 1812.

items.title: Brandenburg Gate
items.text: Once part of the Berlin Wall's border zone, now a symbol of unity.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Bread, sausages, pretzels and sauerkraut are famous, and cakes such as Black Forest gateau are eaten with afternoon coffee.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Germany is the home of composers such as Bach and Beethoven and of the Grimms' fairy tales. Techno music thrives in Berlin.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Christmas markets, with mulled wine and wooden decorations, began in Germany. Carnival is celebrated with parades in the Rhineland.

sport.text: Football is by far the most popular sport. The men's team has won the World Cup four times, in 1954, 1974, 1990 and 2014, and the women's team twice. Germany has also produced Formula 1 champions such as Michael Schumacher and tennis stars such as Steffi Graf.

didYouKnow: Germany has more than 1,500 different kinds of sausage.
The first printed book in Europe using movable type, the Gutenberg Bible, was made in Mainz around 1455.

keyPeople.name: Albert Einstein
keyPeople.text: Born in Ulm in 1879; developed the theory of relativity.

keyPeople.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
keyPeople.text: Wrote some of his greatest music after going deaf.
